Green shapes. Each green is built from two or three overlapping lobes with an uneven edge, so no two match: a kidney wrapped round the hot spring (1), a peanut (2), a crescent round a pot bunker (3), an L (4), a long thin diagonal (5), a clover (6), a long diagonal Redan (7), a bean in the punchbowl (8) and a T below the hall (9). They run from about 460 to 730 m². Every pin is still 3% or less.

Fairway shapes. Each fairway now has two edges set separately along the hole, so it swells where drives land, pinches between landing areas and scallops along its edges. Crevasses and bunkers bite into the edges. Fairways are 50–58 m wide at the drive targets.

Crevasses. Every crevasse now has a jagged, zigzag outline that tapers to a point at each end, and one side is a raised lip of 1.5–4 m with a broken ice face. In the sketches, blue ice walls drop into the dark below a white cornice, so they catch the eye from the tee. On the plans the lip is the heavy edge with ticks.

4, The Crevasse Field. The far side of the last crevasse is now a shelf 4 m higher, a jagged ice face you play up onto. The way round on the right climbs a ramp onto it. The hole now finishes 12 m above the tee.
5, The Seracs. The step between the landing benches is now a jagged ice scarp, 3.5 m high, that zigzags right across the hole. A drive that runs over it drops to the lower bench.

8, The Mammoth. Below the valley step, a long crevasse splits the second leg in two. The high side on its lip is 3 m up, wide and flat, with a view down into the punchbowl. The low side is narrower and runs 15 m closer to the green.
1, 7 and 9. Crevasses with raised lips now bite in at the edges: right of 1's landing area, left of 7's second leg (with cracks splitting off the moulin on the right) and left of 9's second ramp.

Layered scenery. Between the holes and out to the skyline, about 160 more crevasses lie in fields across the ice's flow, with pressure ridges heaped with ice blocks, bands of seracs and nine rock peaks poking through the glacier. All of it stays at least 90 m from every line of play, and the peaks' feet stay 120 m away.
